name: Mozambican Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language: word stress not applicable; only Ngunga et al. 2013 survey report named on Glottolog, no phonology

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page moza1235 (refs: Ngunga et al. 2013; Kamei 2004; Eberhard et al. 2025)
sources.note: No descriptive references; notes LSM is not related to Portuguese Sign Language, possible Finnish SL connection, treated as a presumed isolate.

sources.citation: Xavier, Élio Manuel, Margarida Alberto Teblo & Everson Manjinski. 2025. Análise da implementação da disciplina de Língua de Sinais de Moçambique nos Institutos de Formação de Professores. Teias do Conhecimento. doi:10.5212/revteiasconhecimento.2025.24109
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; teacher-training review. Notes the 2002 dictionary was never formally published because of many errors (per Ngunga et al. 2013) but is still used in the IFPs.

sources.citation: Timbane, Alexandre António. 2024. TV Surdo-Moçambique: buscando acessibilidade e integração do surdo na sociedade. Njinga & Sepé 4(1): 437-454.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/media paper. Names the Ngunga et al. 2013 dictionary (UEM) as the first linguistic instrument for LSM; no structural description.

sources.citation: Jamine, Augusto, Daúda Amisse & Jaime Tai [CORE metadata: Mocumbi, Jaime Tai]. 2021. Configuração das mãos como parâmetro da língua de sinais: um estudo comparativo das Línguas de sinais moçambicana e brasileira. Revista Revise 6 (Fluxo Contínuo 2020: Psicologia e Educação), 232-245. Faculdade de Educação, UEM.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent. Treats the five formational parameters (handshape, movement, facial expression, orientation, location); p.237: 'a entoação nas Línguas de Sinais é feita pela expressão facial'; lists 10 movement types of LSM after Ngunga et al. 2013. Compares 5 handshapes and the manual alphabets of LSM and LIBRAS. Read in full (14 pp).

sources.citation: Bavo, Názia Anita & Orquídea Coelho. 2019. Pertinência e urgência da língua de sinais (L1) e do português (L2/LE) no currículo dos alunos surdos em Moçambique. Revista e-Curriculum 17(3): 909-932. doi:10.23925/1809-3876.2019v17i3p909-932
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; curriculum/education paper. pp.914-915 give the history of the three LSM dictionaries (Pirkko 1995 with Finnish cooperation; Fernando & Bertrand 2002; Ngunga/CEA-UEM 2013, c.1300 entries).

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Mozambican Sign Language'; Wikipedia (pt) 'Língua de sinais moçambicana'
sources.note: No linguistic description; en page cites only Ethnologue 25 (150,000 users, Maputo/Beira/Nampula, some dialectal variation, standardization efforts since 1999); pt page has no sources.

sources.citation: Ngunga, Armindo, Assumane Abudo, David Nhantumbo, Inocêncio Zandamela & Maria Luisa Manguana. 2013. Dicionário da língua de sinais de Moçambique. Maputo: CEA-UEM. 501 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: The only substantial linguistic work on LSM; has an introductory description of the language (definition p.22, inventory of 10 movement types per Jamine et al. 2021). Would confirm whether any prosodic/non-manual remarks exist. Still could not state word stress for a sign language.

sources.citation: Kamei, Nobutaka. 2004. The Sign Languages of Africa. Journal of African Studies (Japan Association for African Studies) 64: 43-64 [as cited on the Glottolog moza1235 page].
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Survey Glottolog cites for LSM's relationship to Portuguese Sign Language; a classification/survey source, not a phonological description.
